title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 32-34). A is a small category. Σ is a class of colimit types (written 𝒞 on p.32) and Σ' a class of limit types (𝒞'). On p.32 Grothendieck looks for an intrinsic subcategory D of Â (or of additive presheaves). D should be stable under Σ-colimits and have Σ'-limits. Every object of D should be both a Σ-colimit of objects of A and a Σ'-limit of such objects. He also gets an 'equivalence remarquable' Â_Σ ≃ ((A°)^_Σ')°. The test case is A with one object and a '½-additive' (preadditive) structure, i.e. a ring k. With Σ = Σ' = finite discrete categories, D is the category of free k-modules of finite type.

This page, opening lines. It finishes the example: free right modules of finite type over k (very probably k = End(A)). Their category is anti-equivalent to the category of free left modules of finite type, by the duality M ↦ Hom_k(M,k).

'Réversion de la condition'. Now assume only that every object of a category C is a Σ-type colimit, taken in C, of objects of A. Let C' be a category in which these (co)limits exist. Let Hom_Σ(C,C') be the full subcategory of functors C→C' preserving them. Grothendieck claims that restriction Hom_Σ(C,C') → Hom(A,C') is fully faithful, with the marginal note 'à vérifier'. He crosses out a stronger claim of equivalence.

Additive specialisation. C is additive and Σ is the finite discrete categories, so every object of C is a finite direct sum of objects of A. For C' additive, Hom_add(C,C') ≃ Hom_½add(A,C'). This is the universal property of the additive envelope (matrix category) of the preadditive category A.

Identifying C. The Yoneda embedding C → Hom_½add(A°,Ab) is fully faithful ('pl. fid.'). C is then identified with the essential image: the additive closure of the representables. This yields (p.34) the equivalence Hom_add(D,C') ≅ Hom_½add(A,C') and its inverse. The inverse gives a pairing D × Hom_½add(A,C') → C', written F⊗_A G. For one object this is the ordinary tensor product of a free right k-module with a left k-object of C'.

Purpose. The point is a general 'Σ-colimit / Σ'-limit envelope' formalism with a duality between the two completions. It is a tool for the dévissage of perfect complexes and multiplicative structures (tensor pairings) in this manuscript.
errors: Full faithfulness of Hom_Σ(C,C') → Hom(A,C') is not automatic merely because each object of C is a Σ-colimit of objects of A. A transformation α on A extends uniquely to each colimit object, but naturality with respect to arbitrary maps a→Y (a in A, Y in C) needs those maps to factor through the colimit diagram of Y. That holds e.g. if A is dense in C, or if objects of A are 'Σ-small'. In the additive finite-sum case it holds because Hom(a, ⊕b_j) = ⊕Hom(a,b_j). Grothendieck's own 'à vérifier' and his crossing-out of the equivalence claim show he was aware of the gap.

Essential surjectivity in the general case also needs existence and choice of colimit presentations. This is fine in the additive case (functors on Mat(A) are determined by additivity), which is the case he actually uses.

ideas.what: Universal property: additive functors out of the additive envelope of a preadditive ('½-additive') category A ≃ additive functors out of A
ideas.modern_name: Additive envelope / Mat(A) universal property; free completion under finite biproducts
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; enriched form in Kelly, Basic Concepts of Enriched Category Theory (1982)

ideas.what: Restriction from Σ-colimit-preserving functors on a category generated under Σ-colimits by A is fully faithful
ideas.modern_name: Free Φ-cocompletion / closure of A under a class of colimits
ideas.where_published: Related themes in SGA4 Exp. I (ind-objects, Kan extensions)

ideas.what: Duality of finitely generated free right and left modules as an instance of a duality between a Σ-colimit envelope and a Σ'-limit envelope
ideas.modern_name: Cauchy completion / absolute colimits; Isbell-type duality between completions

ideas.what: Tensor pairing D × Hom_½add(A,C') → C', F⊗_A G, induced by the inverse of the restriction equivalence
ideas.modern_name: Functor tensor product / coend; weighted colimit

ideas.what: Terminology '½-additive' for preadditive (Ab-enriched without biproducts) categories

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a general framework of envelopes in which every object is simultaneously a Σ-colimit and a Σ'-limit of objects of A, with an equivalence Â_Σ ≃ ((A°)^_Σ')°. He tests it only in the finite-biproduct case and leaves the general full-faithfulness 'à vérifier'. The general bi-completion and duality question was not completed here.
missed.quote: on trouve que Hom_Σ'(C,C') → Hom(A,C') ... à vérifier ... est pl. fidèle
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is close to later work on closures under classes of colimits and on absolute (Cauchy) colimits. The page itself is mostly standard; the novelty, if any, lies in the planned two-sided (colimit/limit) envelope, likely already subsumed by Kelly-school results.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is standard (additive envelope universal property, Yoneda, functor tensor product). The general framework is anticipatory but was soon or already developed by Lawvere, Street and Kelly. The interest is mainly historical: Grothendieck's private use of such tools around 1975-76.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'h = Σ-ad(A)' is very likely 'k = End(A)' (the ring of the single object A, continuing the free k-module example of p.32).
'Un type de C est une Lim de C de type Σ'' should read 'Un objet de C est une Lim dans C de type Σ (or Σ') d'objets de A'.
'catégorie C' à limites exactes' is probably 'soit C' une catégorie où ces limites existent' (partly crossed out).
'C --plft--> Hom_½add(A°,Ab)' : the label is 'pl. fid.' (pleinement fidèle).
'En rappelant de l'inclusion' is probably 'En utilisant l'inclusion'.
'déduisant par DC l'image essentielle' is probably 'désignant par D l'image essentielle' (consistent with D on the next page).
The margin note 'à vérifier' is attached to the full-faithfulness claim. The crossed-out continuation is '[et ... équivalence de cat. si ... C ... lim]'.
